summary: _in terms of the Letter of Intent dated 05.02.2024, 02.02.2024, and 01.02.2024 issued under the SHAKTI Policy;_ _(b) Pass such other and further order or orders as this Commission deems appropriate under the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ 2. The Petitioner, Adhunik Power & Natural Resources Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956, has set up a Thermal Power Project with an installed capacity of 540 MW (2 x 270 MW) (‘the Project’) at SaraikelaKharsawn District in the State of Jharkhand. The Petitioner is a generating company within the meaning of Section 2(28) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’). 5. Accordingly, Central Coalfields Limited (CCL) issued the Letter of Intent (LOI) dated 21.12.2017, declaring the Petitioner as the Provisional successful bidder and allocating 900,000 tonnes of coal (G 11 grade) per annum against the abovementioned PPAs as well as 122.85 MW PPA with Jharkhand Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited (JBVNL), with whom the Petitioner also has executed a long-term PPA. 6. The Petitioner has submitted that pursuant to the issuance of the LOI dated 21.12.2017, the Petitioner executed a supplementary/amended PPA dated 10.5.2018 & 8.5.2018 in order to incorporate the necessary changes in the aforesaid PPAs executed between the Petitioner and Respondent 2 and Respondent 1 and Respondent 2 herein, after approval of this Commission for the discount in tariff offered by the Petitioner, vide Order dated 18.5.2018 read with corrigendum dated 17.7.2018 passed in Petition No. 84/MP/2018. 7. The Petitioner has submitted that on 8.1.2020, Power Finance Corporation Limited, a Govt. of India Undertaking (“PFC”), issued a request for submission of the expression of interest for the third round of auction of coal linkages under paragraph b(ii) of the SHAKTI Scheme for the IPPs having already concluded long term PPAs (“Third Round Auction”). The Petitioner participated in the Third Round Auction, further to the Procurer PPA/APNRL-PTC PPA as well as 122.85 MW JBVNL PPA and offered 8 paise/kWh as discount and was declared as a provisional successful bidder vide LOI dated 14.7.2020, issued by the Central Coalfields Limited for the award of the 99,000 tonne quantity of coal on an annual basis in relation to the Procurer PPA/APNRL-PTC PPA as well as 122.85 MW JBVNL PPA. 9. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that pursuant to issuance of the LOI dated 26.11.2021 and 25.11.2021, the Petitioner executed a supplementary/amended PPA dated 9.3.2022 in order to incorporate the necessary changes in the aforesaid PPAs executed between the Petitioner and Respondent 2 and Respondent 1 and Respondent 2 herein, after approval of this Commission for the discount in tariff offered by the Petitioner, vide Order dated 3.6.2022 passed in Petition No. 129/MP/2022. 11. In light of the aforesaid, the Petitioner has prayed for approval of the aforementioned addendums to the Power Purchase Agreements incorporating the aforementioned discounts in tariff. 12. The Petitioner has stated that it is supplying power to the distribution licensees situated in more than one State by execution of (a) the PPA dated 28.9.2012 with JBVNL for supply of the 122.85 MW (b) PPA dated 25.3.2011 for supply of the 100 MW to WBSEDCL through PTC on back to back basis and (c) PPA dated 19.12.2013 for supply of the 100 MW to TANGEDCO through PTC on back to back basis. Accordingly, the Petitioner has submitted that it has a composite scheme for the supply of power in more than one State in terms of Section 79(1)(b) of the Electricity Act, 2003. Hence, the Petitioner has submitted that in terms of the decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the Energy Watchdog case, the Commission has the jurisdiction to regulate the tariff of the Petitioner. 16. The Petitioner, vide its affidavit dated 1.5.2024, has submitted the informed called for. Respondent 1, vide its affidavit dated 14.5.2024, has submitted that the Respondent, TAGNEDCO, has agreed to the relief prayed for by the Petitioner and has no objections to the contents of the detail submitted by the Petitioner on 1.5.2024. 17. As stated in paragraph 12 above, the Petitioner has entered into PPAs with the distribution licensees, namely, TANGEDCO, WBSEDCL, and JBVNL, i.e., the discoms of the three States, for the supply of power at different points in time and for ‐ different quantum. Sub section (b) of Section 79(1) of the Act provides that the Central Commission shall regulate the tariff of the generating company if such generating company enters into or otherwise has a composite scheme for the generation and sale of electricity in more than one State. The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide its judgment dated 11.4.2017 in Civil Appeals titled Energy Watchdog v CERC & ors [(2017 (4) SCALE 580)] has explained the composite scheme and decided the jurisdiction of this Commission for regulating the tariff of projects meeting the composite scheme as under: In light of the decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, this Commission has the jurisdiction to regulate the tariff of the Petitioner’s Project under Section 79(1)(b) of the Act since, in terms of the PPAs entered into, the Project of the Petitioner has a composite scheme for generation and sale of electricity in more than one state. _iii. FSA shall be signed with the successful bidders after the terms and conditions for signing of FSA are met and the Appropriate Commission has approved the amendment or supplement to the PPA._ per Letter of Intent dated 1.2.2024, 2.2.2024, and 5.2.2024 (13 paise/ kWh) for the Respondent, TANGEDCO, is adopted in terms of Section 63 of Act.
title: Petition under 79 (1)(b) and (f) for approval of the discount in tariff on account of allocation of coal linkage under the SHAKTI Scheme of the Government of India. Adhunik Power and Natural Resources Limited
